Having a US business, bank account and so on makes you a 'US person' in the eyes of the US government which comes with downsides, like banks refusing you as a customer elsewhere.
I live in Algeria, and we can't use credit cards here... This is a great use case for my country and great initiative from Stripe.
Currently, a Canadian business can accept $USD with Stripe and have it deposited directly into a Canadian US fund account without conversion to CAD... That process is what Stripe Atlas simplifies.
$500 is a great deal for an LLC with a fully vetted operating agreement suited for an internet company as well as a bank account out of the box.
llc setup cost is $50, bank accounts, stripe accounts are all free, same goes for any credits from aws and elsewhere. I understand the desire to turn a profit on this, but that's kind of overboard.
What you're paying for isn't the paperwork and filing fees, it's the access to lawyers and tax help and the network of other founders... I'd say it's worth it.

Heads up, if you're not a US citizen, Azlo (the underlying checking account provider they use) doesn't let you open an account... they definitely don't let their regular customers through without a US passport.

Closed the SVB account month two of the company. Opened an account with Capital One Spark Business, no minimum fees and the customer service has been good... Stripe should really partner with a better bank.
I found the customer support incredible helpful. Whenever I had questions, I would always get a response within 24 hours... I strongly feel Atlas is a very good product.
I've had a good experience with it, except that I agree the migrating to a new Stripe account was a big pain. It's really not clear to me why Stripe couldn't just add Atlas to your existing account.
SVB is a bit annoying, but really $25/month is probably not worth your time to worry about... With the AWS credits and how generally easy it was, I would definitely recommend it.
SVB sucks, true. But $300/yr for a bank account should not be a deal breaker... Atlas also made filing 2017 taxes trivial, I never even spoke to an accountant, it was a very smooth process.

I completely disagree with this post. I setup an LLC late last year and it was a very pleasant experience via Atlas. They clearly show a checklist of what you need to do... I would definitely do it again.
As a foreign founder, I personally went through Stripe Atlas last month, no regrets at all. The whole process took longer than I expected but it's not their problem... solid customer service.
If you're not in the US, Azlo doesn't even support international transfers. They do not have login system for multiple founders... require SSN to open an account.

I set up an LLC via Atlas. The process was simple, but there's a lot of legwork at the state/city level that they don't do and you'll need to be prepared to do yourself. Atlas does not remove the need for an accountant, or a lawyer.
We really wanted to use Stripe Atlas for our startup but ended up using Clerky for various reasons... Atlas is getting closer and closer to closing all the gaps.

Used Atlas to incorporate and they helped correct mistakes that were made on both ends, was really nice having an actual person to talk to. Also had a deal for reduced fees which made it even sweeter.

Atlas companies are optimized to 'receive investments' where it's setup with a high share count which attracts obscenely large Delaware franchise tax bills... You have to be proactive about adjusting for this on your own, there were no warnings.

Their choice for using SVB as your companies preferred no-frills bank is also puzzling, it's slow, has a horrible UX, never improves, constant planned maintenance downtimes... the opposite you'd expect from a Stripe UX.
